items.title: Putin, Trump and Xi discuss Ukraine at trilateral meeting
items.summary: President Vladimir Putin said Russia, China and the United States share interests in resolving regional conflicts, including the war in Ukraine. President Donald Trump said the leaders would discuss Ukraine and nuclear arms reductions, while Xi Jinping called cooperation among the three powers essential for global stability. No settlement was announced in the reported opening remarks.

items.title: Kursk governor reports nine injured in Ukrainian drone strikes
items.summary: Regional authorities said nine people were injured in drone attacks on Kursk, including a 12-year-old rescued from the rubble of a private home. Officials reported damage to residential buildings, a court, a library, a medical college and vehicles, with several cars catching fire.

items.title: Crimea says rail traffic on damaged bridge may resume at 16:00
items.summary: Crimean leader Sergey Aksyonov said train service across the Crimean Bridge was expected to resume around 16:00 local time on November 19 after the latest reported Ukrainian attack. Railway crews were assessing and repairing damage, and authorities said alternative passenger routes would be published.

items.title: Russia receives new batch of Su-57 fighter jets
items.summary: Russia's United Aircraft Corporation delivered another batch of Su-57 fighters to the Aerospace Forces, according to Rostec. The aircraft reportedly completed factory and military acceptance tests; officials said the type has been used during the war in Ukraine, but did not disclose the number delivered.

items.title: Russian diplomat says German political will needed to restart Nord Stream gas
items.summary: Deputy Foreign Minister Dmitry Lyubinsky said resuming Russian gas supplies to Germany through an intact Nord Stream pipeline would require political willingness from Berlin, which he said was absent. He also accused German authorities of failing to cooperate with Russia over the pipeline sabotage investigation; those criticisms reflect Moscow's position.
